business_scope.primary_industry_name: Track Laying and Overhead Catenary Power for Metro Tram Networks

stage_1.jurisdiction_name_en: Egypt (national, unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
stage_1.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law legal system (French-inspired codified framework) with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation under Article 2 of the 2014 Constitution; unitary national regulatory regime administered by GAFI under the ambit of the Ministry of Investment and the Ministry of Justice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agadir Agreement: Egypt-Jordan-Morocco-Tunisia Free Trade Area (2007)
Greater Arab Free Trade Area (GAFTA), in force 2005
Unified Agreement for Investment of Arab Capital in the Arab States (1980)
Egypt-United Kingdom Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 1976)
Egypt-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (in force 1999)
Egypt-United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement (in force 1980)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018 and Investment Law No. 72 of 2017; Limited Liability Company provisions governed by Articles 102–134 of the Companies Law, together with GAFI Executive Regulations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Division, One-Stop Shop, Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application Form together with notarized Articles of Association (Aware El-Taasis), adopted and filed through the GAFI One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981. Quotas must be fully subscribed and paid up as stated in the Articles of Association. No escrow account is statutorily required, provided capital contributions are evidenced by bank receipt or in-kind appraisal; foreign capital contributions for the EPC project may require transfer confirmation from a licensed Egyptian bank under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the company acknowledges its incorporation as an Egyptian Limited Liability Company under Law No. 159 of 1981 and adopts the Articles of Association as filed with GAFI. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the members approve the subscription and allocation of quotas as set out in the capital schedule, and that all subscription amounts have been duly contributed. RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be established at the address listed in the Articles and may be relocated by future resolution. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed General Manager, [Name] be appointed Financial Officer, and [Name] be appointed Compliance Officer with full signatory authority in their respective capacities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Form Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop / GAFI Commercial Names Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the requested trade name in both Arabic and English through the GAFI online portal. Verify that the name does not conflict with prior registered marks or state-owned names. The LLC legal form indicator must be stated in the name. Pay the reservation fee and obtain the name availability certificate before preparing incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Requested name(s) in Arabic and English
Professional form submission through GAFI e-portal
Copy of applicant national ID or passport
Authorization letter if submitted by agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit alternative names through the grievance channel within 15 days, or file a formal objection with GAFI Legal Affairs Department with supporting trademark/search evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Attestation of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public / GAFI Approved Legal Drafting Counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Egyptian attorney to draft the Articles of Association (Aware El-Taasis) in Arabic. The Articles must state the LLC name, registered office, purpose, capital, number of quotas, subscription method, management structure, and dispute resolution clause. All founding members or their authorized representatives must sign before the Notary Public. The notarization attested by counsel and members.
required_dossiers: Fully signed Articles of Association (3 copies)
Power of attorney for each non-resident founder (if any)
Passport or national ID copies of all founders
Draft of LLC quota allocation schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the Notary Public requests corrections, revise Articles and re-attest. If stale name or address appears, obtain supplementary resolution from founders to amend the affected article.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Contribution Verification and Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Egyptian Bank / Commercial Bank Capital Unit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account under the proposed LLC name and deposit the declared paid-up capital. Obtain a bank certificate confirming receipt of the capital in Egyptian pounds or foreign currency. For in-kind contributions, obtain a valuation report approved by the founders and GAFI guidelines. The certificate must refer to the LLC name and the names of all contributing members.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests amendments, align the deposit receipt with the final Articles wording. Missing foreign transfer documentation may be cured by obtaining the SWIFT credit advice and a legalized source-of-funds letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Statutory Filing and Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Companies Filing Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Electronically or physically submit the attested Articles, bank certificate, name reservation certificate, and incorporation application to GAFI. Complete all applicable disclosure forms for shareholders, managers, and registered office. After review, GAFI will issue the Incorporation Certificate and assign the legal entity number. Pay the statutory filing fee and any publication fees.
required_dossiers: No-objection letters from relevant professional or industrial authorities (if activity requires prior approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a deficiency query, cure the deficiency within 15 days. Re-submission accepted with an explanatory cover letter. If the application is rejected, file an internal grievance before GAFI within 30 days and, if needed, initiate administrative appeal before the State Council.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Trade and Industry) / Egyptian Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI incorporation approval, register the LLC in the Commercial Register at the local commercial registry office. Submit the incorporation certificate and Articles of Association. Concurrently apply to the Egyptian Tax Authority for the Tax Card, declaring the anticipated rail EPC activity, VAT obligations, and payroll. Obtain the tax identification number and prepare for inspection by the Tax Authority.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered office lease or land ownership document
Bank account statement proving capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry notes discrepancies, file amended memorandum with GAFI and then resubmit to the registry. For Tax Card delays, escalate through the Tax Authority service center; submit an official tracing request and retain provisional payment receipts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal Management / GAFI Records / Licensed Bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the First Board Resolution, open the permanent corporate bank account, obtain the corporate seal, create the statutory quota ledger, and appoint the external auditor. File any manager or director changes with GAFI. Ensure registered office lease is available, the corporate address is displayed, and all books are pre-stamped by the Commercial Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires additional beneficiary ownership clearance, provide a GAFI legal entity report and a board resolution identifying the ultimate beneficial owner. For GAFI record mismatches, submit a rectification petition with supporting resolutions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – Engineering and Rail Systems Licensing Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating License for Rail Transit Infrastructure Manufacturing and EPC Support Works (License No. 15 of 2017 Industrial Licensing Law)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Environmental Impact Screening and Scoping required for light rail transit EPC and associated construction/manufacturing activities; full Category A EIA required if works are located in urban sensitive zones, near water bodies, or involve heavy industrial fabrication facilities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Law No. 4 of 1994 and Ministerial Decree No. 1 of 2001: wastewater BOD not exceeding 60 mg/l, COD not exceeding 130 mg/l, TSS not exceeding 80 mg/l; air particulate matter not exceeding 60 µg/m3 for PM10; VOC controls for catenary coating and welding operations using integrated abatement systems; solid hazardous waste must be stored, labeled, and manifested through EEAA and the Industrial Development Authority; stormwater discharge from railyards and workshops must meet Department of Sanitation prescribed limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate from the Civil Defense Authority (Ministry of Interior) under Law No. 41 of 1971, including approved egress plans, extinguishing systems, and storage segregation for welding gases and solvents; Structural Load Inspection and building completion clearance from the local municipality certifying permanent workshops, laydown areas, and offices; Occupational Safety and Health Clearance from the Ministry of Manpower under Law No. 12 of 2003 covering workplace hazard assessment, electrical safety, and mandatory training of construction and rail personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egypt Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; national unified taxpayer registration and e-filing portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoice clearance and e-receipt portal: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute and notarize the LLC Memorandum of Association and register the EG LLC via the GAFI one-stop shop under Companies Law 159/1981 and Investment Law 72/2017, obtaining the Commercial Registry extract and manager identification documents. Step 2: Submit to the ETA within 30 days of commercial registration a unified tax-registration application (Tax Card application) containing the commercial registry extract, notarized constitutional documents, board appointment resolution, head-office lease, and manager IDs; the ETA then issues the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Single Unified Tax Registration certificate. Step 3: The same tax file is activated automatically for corporate income tax, VAT, and stamp tax, and a VAT registration certificate is issued where mandatory registration applies or upon voluntary election. Step 4: Activate ETA e-invoicing credentials (digital signature, API token, and QR-stamp keys) in the e-invoicing portal. Step 5: Open a corporate EGP/FX bank account at an authorized Egyptian bank and file the export-customs and inward-remittance codes with the bank for future FX repatriation compliance; a licensed tax accountant must be appointed as the legal tax representative before ETA correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the Egyptian LLC is a juridical person and full Egyptian tax resident taxed on worldwide income under Law 91/2005, as amended by Law 26/2020, at 22.5% corporate income tax on taxable income up to EGP 80 million and 32.5% on the excess; no pass-through or US-style disregarded-entity treatment is available, and free-zone classifications apply only where an explicit GAFI/SCZone investment license is granted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a check-the-box election; juridical classification is fixed by statute. Available elections include: (i) fiscal-year election — adoption of any 12-month tax period with ETA approval, defaulting to the calendar year; (ii) SME presumptive tax regime election under Law 152/2020 for annual turnover not exceeding EGP 20 million, replacing corporation tax, stamp duties, and public levies with turnover-based brackets; (iii) free-zone/SCZone license election substituting 0% corporate income tax during the licensed period for an annual board fee in foreign currency; (iv) unincorporated joint-venture election under Law 91/2005 to treat jointly-owned project structures as a single taxable unit; and (v) no hybrid-mismatch organized election — Egypt's CFC rules and general anti-avoidance clause override artificial arrangements lacking economic substance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) — Law No. 67 of 2016, effective 8 September 2016, replacing the prior Sales Tax; implementing rules set out in Prime Ministerial Decree No. 66 of 2017, as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 of annual taxable supplies of goods or services triggering mandatory VAT registration under Law 67/2016 and Executive Regulations; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold, and non-resident suppliers making taxable supplies in Egypt must register and appoint an Egyptian tax representative
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time e-invoicing applies to VAT-registered businesses under ETA Decree No. 420/2020 and subsequent amendments. Every tax invoice must be issued through the ETA centralized clearance platform or a certified ERP-to-API integration; the ETA validates invoice data in near real time and returns a digital stamp comprising a unique invoice UUID and QR code, which is embedded before issuance to the buyer. Un-cleared invoices are legally invalid and the transaction is treated as undocumented; since 2022, the parallel B2C e-receipt system is mandatory in phased waves. System non-compliance results in blocked invoice issuance, fines under the VAT law, and referral to the ETA audit division.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT under Law 67/2016 applies to: (i) export of goods — title passes to a non-resident buyer, goods physically leave Egypt under a valid customs export declaration within 180 days from the invoice date, and proceeds are credited to an Egyptian authorized bank in freely convertible foreign currency; and (ii) exported services — services supplied to a non-resident, performed and effectively used outside Egypt, and covered by the Executive Regulations' list of zero-rated offshore services (including engineering, design, telecommunication, transportation, and ancillary logistics). For the Urban Light Rail Transit EPC scope, only separable offshore design-engineering and offshore procurement segments may qualify for 0%; on-site track laying, catenary installation, and local construction within Egypt remain standard-rated at 14%, so each zero-rated invoice must be traceable to a distinct offshore work-package in the EPC contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (ECS/C88 document) stamped by the Egyptian Customs Authority evidencing physical exit of the goods from Egypt within the statutory 180-day window
Original Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR road consignment note consigned to the non-resident buyer and cross-referenced to the invoice, contract, and customs export declaration
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/telex credit advice from an authorized Egyptian bank evidencing receipt and conversion of the export proceeds in freely convertible foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA audits export files within the five-year assessment period. If the customs exit proof, shipping document, or FX inward remittance is defective or the 180-day repatriation deadline is missed, the 0% rate is reversed retroactively and 14% output VAT is assessed from the original invoice date, plus a delay penalty of 1.5% per month on the unpaid tax (18% per annum). Where export documentation is fabricated or input VAT has been recovered on a false export claim, the conduct qualifies as VAT evasion under Article 72 of Law 67/2016, carrying imprisonment and fines of EGP 5,000 to EGP 50,000 in addition to full clawback of credited input VAT; the Income Tax Law adds an additional charge of up to 200% of the evaded tax on falsified export declarations, and the Central Bank of Egypt may suspend the authorized bank's export-processing privileges for foreign-exchange rule breaches.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) - the sole monetary authority and foreign exchange regulator under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), exercising exchange controls through its General Department of Foreign Exchange and the Banking Supervision AML/CFT Unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt maintains Article VIII current-account convertibility under the IMF Articles of Agreement; the EGP was fully floated on 6 March 2024 under the CBE exchange-rate unification decision, removing former conversion queues and documentary rationing. Dividend and profit remittance by a Limited Liability Company is legally guaranteed and non-discretionary, but operationally conditioned on (i) audited financial statements prepared under Egyptian GAAP or IFRS, (ii) a tax clearance certificate issued by the Egyptian Tax Authority, and (iii) availability of EGP funds at a CBE-licensed remitting bank; no separate CBE approval is required for current-account profit transfers below the statutory reporting threshold. Capital-account outflows, including shareholder loan principal and equity liquidation proceeds, require proof that the underlying inward transaction was registered with the CBE or the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) at entry to evidence legal repatriability.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory export-proceeds surrender regime was abolished by the CBE exchange-rate unification circular of 6 March 2024; no fixed conversion ratio or statutory surrender window currently applies to export receipts. Exporters must nevertheless credit proceeds to an exporter's foreign-currency account at a licensed Egyptian bank within the settlement tenor stated in the underlying commercial terms, normally 30 to 60 days from the bill of lading, via SWIFT transfer, and must support the receipt within five business days with the Nafeza/ACID customs export declaration and commercial invoice so that the bank can file the CBE export-proceeds report. Failure to credit proceeds within the agreed letter-of-credit or Incoterms period triggers CBE irregular-settlement reporting and may disqualify the entity from access to import financing facilities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + EGP/FCY Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account + EGP/FCY Operational Account
Operational Account with segregated Capital Escrow sub-account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs regulated in the UK, EU, or Singapore are not recognised by the CBE as settlement banks in Egypt; using an unlicensed EMI to hold the LLC's operating liquidity would breach the Banking Law deposit-taking monopoly and the payment-fintech licensing regime of Law No. 5 of 2022 unless the EMI operates through an Egyptian-registered subsidiary holding a CBE licence. Commercial viability is LOW as a primary clearing rail: acceptable only as an ancillary payment-card or virtual-IBAN receiving tool, while all EPC contract settlement, government bond escrow flows, and CBE balance-of-payments-visible liquidity must reside at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory: at least one authorised signatory, or the Egyptian resident manager where a power of attorney is used, must appear in person at the branch for the compliance interview, signature specimen verification, and beneficial-ownership walk-through. Fully remote or digital corporate account opening is not available for a foreign-owned LLC under current CBE AML/KYC guidance; non-resident directors may be represented only through a consular-legalised power of attorney in favour of the resident manager. The opening package must include the original Commercial Registry extract, tax card, company seal specimen, certified board resolutions, and the complete CBE UBO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain passing through a trust, foundation, or a jurisdiction with deficient AML enforcement, which would negate the low-risk classification of the EPC entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalised series of corporate registry extracts with apostille certification, completed Egypt UBO declaration form, six months of bank statements of the foreign parent covering the initial capital injection amount, notarised source-of-wealth statement for each UBO, and an Egyptian counsel legal opinion confirming the absence of shell-entity indicators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value government-linked infrastructure contract with milestone escrow and sovereign counterparty, creating elevated procurement-corruption and economic-sanctions-subversion risk in underwriting review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EPC or concession contract, the sovereign guarantee or government bond escrow instruments, the government-side mandate letter, an intermediary and commission disclosure deed identifying every agent and consultancy, and the bank's public-procurement integrity questionnaire signed by all LLC board members.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First large inbound wire arriving without matching the project milestone schedule or the LLC's declared paid-up capital, causing transaction-velocity deviation and source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pre-approved project cash-flow model lodged at account opening, each inbound payment matched to a work-stage certificate and supplier invoice, Customs ACID import and Nafeza export declarations within five business days of each flow, and a standing escalation undertaking with the relationship officer for any out-of-pattern funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP status of a shareholder, director, or the Egyptian state counterparty's procurement officer, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential reputational conflict in the EPC award.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP declaration and source-of-funds statement, an enhanced monitoring acceptance letter subjecting the account to ongoing transaction analysis, corporate resolutions restricting the PEP role to non-procurement board functions, and a legal opinion confirming the absence of any public-official interest in the EPC supply chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections must be wired by SWIFT MT103 from the parent to the LLC's account at a CBE-licensed Egyptian bank, or by MT202 for interbank reallocation, quoting the GAFI registration number and the bank customer-information file reference; the receiving bank credits the foreign-currency sub-account or converts the principal to EGP at the prevailing interbank market rate. The bank retains the inward SWIFT reference, issues the CBE investment-transfer form as proof of conversion, and reports values above USD 100,000 or EGP equivalent to the CBE through its electronic Balance-of-Payments reporting interface to establish the repatriation file. Government bond escrow receipts funded by the Egyptian state counterparty under the EPC concession are settled directly on the statutory escrow bank ledger, typically at NBE or Banque Misr, and are confirmed to the LLC and any senior lender through a bank-to-bank SWIFT advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier settlements are executed by SWIFT MT103 from the Egyptian bank under a back-to-back documentary facility, or under a commercial letter of credit governed by UCP600 and confirmed through a foreign correspondent using the MT700/MT798 messaging chain; the bank requires proforma invoices, the ACID/Nafeza customs import declaration, and for plant and equipment the relevant import-financing notices before releasing hard currency. Dividend and profit repatriation to foreign shareholders follows the same MT103 rail after delivery of the tax clearance certificate and audited financial statements, while share-capital repatriation additionally requires the historical CBE registration evidence of the original inward injection and proof of full settlement of Egyptian taxes. All outflows are pre-funded in EGP and sold into hard currency at the interbank market rate prevailing on execution date.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward for genuine EPC trade or investment exposure, with tenor aligned to the underlying milestone maturity and fully collateralised by the project receivable; this is the standard corporate hedging product available after the 2024 CBE foreign-exchange liberalisation.

FX swap, also referred to as cross-currency swap, contracted bilaterally with a licensed Egyptian bank for cash-flow matching of EGP revenue into EUR or USD procurement spend; such swap must be net-settled on actual delivery rather than settled as an offshore hedge.
Spot FX outright at CBE interbank market rates for day-to-day trade settlement, requiring the presentation of underlying transaction documentation but no prior CBE approval.

Currency options, available only as interbank or bank-to-bank instruments; Egyptian non-financial corporate end-users are not currently a standard product segment for option products under CBE governance.

Non-deliverable forward, not permissible onshore; an offshore NDF booking through a foreign affiliate of the Egyptian bank may operate as a credit-risk-neutral mechanism but is unenforceable against the Egyptian bank and requires a formal legal opinion from the offshore booking jurisdiction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Arabic language tax declaration and supporting schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 30 April of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 20% of assessed tax, increasing to 40% after formal demand and up to 100% for concealment; monthly late-payment interest applies. Timeline triggering administrative strike-off: two consecutive years of non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement, notes, and auditor's report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and Commercial Registry Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Partners' approval within 3 months of financial year-end; filing with the Commercial Registry within 30 days of approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Refusal to register new corporate entries, blocking amendment or share-transfer filings, and disqualification from GAFI investment incentives; directors become personally liable. Timeline triggering administrative strike-off: failure to deposit audited financial statements for two consecutive fiscal years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO and Shareholding Confirmation Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority / GAFI AML Compliance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 April for a 31 December year-end; within 30 days of any share-transfer event changing beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML non-compliance fines of up to EGP 1,000,000 and suspension of the company's active status in ETA/GAFI portals. Timeline triggering administrative strike-off: outstanding UBO confirmation for two consecutive annual cycles.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Egyptian LLC is required to appoint at least one licensed external auditor for its annual financial statements under Companies Law 159/1981; the Egyptian Tax Authority additionally requires independently audited statements when paid-up capital exceeds EGP 500,000 or annual turnover exceeds EGP 5,000,000.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), mandatory for statutory accounts and harmonized with IFRS; consolidated financial statements follow IFRS/EAS as required by the Financial Regulatory Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, before the CIT deadline, the LLC must confirm its current beneficial-ownership register via the ETA tax-return declaration, identifying all natural persons holding 10% or more or exercising ultimate control. Any share-transfer-induced change must be reported to GAFI and the Commercial Registry within 30 days of execution; UBO data is maintained in the secure ETA/GAFI corporate portal and is not public.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–1,400 per annum for a physical registered office and corporate agent in Cairo or Alexandria; USD 1,200–2,200 with administrative support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–8,000 per annum depending on EPC project volume and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% unified corporate income tax on net taxable income of juridical persons under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended by Law No. 26 of 2020.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Eligible urban light-rail infrastructure EPC projects may deduct up to 50% of qualifying investment costs from taxable profit for 7 consecutive years under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, subject to the 80%-of-net-profit cap. Accelerated depreciation applies to track-laying machinery, catenary installation equipment, and rolling stock. Licensed Free-Zone entrants may elect the annual flat Free-Zone fee regime in lieu of CIT. Suez Canal Economic Zone projects may access a 50% tax-base reduction for a defined incentive period. The statutory headline rate remains 22.5%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return for Juridical Persons Form No. 21, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at eta.gov.eg. The return must be accompanied by the mandatory Transfer Pricing Annexure and the Financial Statements pack. A licensed Egyptian tax agent or the resident representative performs the filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return with interim advance payments of estimated CIT during the fiscal year as assessed by the ETA. The ETA Large Taxpayer Center may impose monthly provisional CIT collections on public-sector EPC contract receipts.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Submission and full settlement within the four months following the fiscal year-end under Article 46 of Law No. 91 of 2005. For a 31 December balance-sheet date, the deadline is 30 April. A reasoned 60-day extension may be requested from the competent ETA directorate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: legal name, Tax Card number, commercial registration number, address, and ETA tax-office code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian permanent establishment registration number and the branch address of the PE; attach the standing power of attorney to the resident representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable fiscal period from/to and principal activity classification code (ISIC 4210 Rail Construction and Urban Light Rail Transit EPC).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE operation commencement date and the actual duration of contract site activity inside Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: EPC contract value recognized, variation orders, escalation payments, retention money released, and government bond escrow draws.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Egypt-sourced revenue attributable to the PE under Article 56 allocation rules; exclude home-office procurement invoices.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct contract costs: imported rail steel, ballast, catenary wire, subcontractor labour, plant hire, equipment depreciation, and site establishment costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party subcontracting must be priced at arm's length under the TP rules; attach invoice-to-BOQ mapping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating and administrative expenses: rent, utilities, engineering payroll, insurance, warranties, and amortization of project licenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Head-office overhead allocations require a documented arm's-length cost-sharing agreement and identical treatment in the home-jurisdiction return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expense add-backs: self-assessed VAT, penalties, bribes, client entertainment above statutory limits, and contingent liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same add-back rules apply to the PE; the PE must not deduct home-office income taxes or shareholder-level expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transaction and transfer-pricing annex: aggregate value of controlled purchases, sales, loans, royalty payments, and head-office charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the foreign related counterparty, jurisdiction, and selected TP method; attach the Master File and Local File once thresholds are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax loss carry-forward deduction: losses utilized from the prior 5-year horizon, supported by final assessments of the loss years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE losses may be carried forward only against future profits of the same Egyptian branch activity, never against foreign head-office income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after investment incentives: 50% investment-cost deduction under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and any Free-Zone fee set-off, capped at 80% of net profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The incentive applies only to assets physically located in Egypt and registered in the PE's fixed-asset register.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computation: taxable income at 22.5%, reduced by foreign tax credits and interim CIT instalments already paid, resulting in the balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax credits are allowed only if the Egyptian payment account confirms retention at source; final balance is payable before the four-month deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed fine of EGP 500 to EGP 5,000 under Article 133(1) of Law 91 of 2005, plus a 2%-per-commenced-month deferment surcharge on the unpaid tax. The outstanding balance also bears interest at the Central Bank of Egypt discount rate plus 2% per annum. False declarations trigger Article 134 criminal penalties, automatic travel-ban proceedings, and loss of voluntary-disclosure leniency.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders under Article 111 of Law No. 91 of 2005, applied after CIT at the distributing LLC level. Resident corporate shareholders that own at least 25% for two years qualify for the domestic participation exemption. Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to the domestic exemption unless a treaty grants a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Egypt maintains a broad DTA network. To invoke treaty relief: (1) obtain an annual Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (2) apostille or consular-legalize the TRC, translate it into Arabic, and certify the beneficial owner of the shares; (3) file the ETA Treaty-Relief Application through the e-filing portal before the dividend distribution, attaching the shareholder register, shareholding tenure, and substance evidence; (4) obtain ETA written clearance; (5) if relief was not granted on time, reclaim the excess WHT within the 5-year limitation period through the ETA Audit and Appeal procedure. The MLI Principal Purpose Test applies, so the recipient must demonstrate substantive business activity in the treaty state.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for catenary design models, track-laying patents, and EPC software attract a statutory 20% WHT; treaty rates usually range from 10% to 15%. Interest paid to non-resident lenders attracts a statutory 20% WHT, reduced to 0% for Central Bank of Egypt-registered commercial lending and export-financing facilities; DTA rates commonly range from 5% to 10%. Interest embedded in a government bond escrow structure must be documented as genuine debt, not equity, to avoid recharacterization as a dividend subject to 10% WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 of aggregate related-party transactions within a fiscal year triggers the mandatory TP annexure and Local File preparation. An MNE group with consolidated turnover above EGP 200,000,000 must also prepare a Master File. The ETA may lower the thresholds on a risk-based selection for rail-infrastructure contractors.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP: preferred for standard rail materials, steel, and equipment purchases
Resale Price Method: subcontractor and trader distribution margins
Cost Plus Method: integrated EPC assembly and site installation
TNMM: functional analysis of the Egyptian LLC as the tested party
Transactional Profit Split: joint engineering, procurement, and construction risk-sharing contracts
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt applies the OECD-BEPS substance-over-form doctrine through Article 36 GAAR of Law No. 91 of 2005 and the MLI Principal Purpose Test. A non-resident controlling the Egyptian EPC LLC must demonstrate real business presence, qualified engineers, site-supervision capacity, equipment ownership, insurable risk, and strategic decision-making in the treaty state. Egypt does not maintain a codified ESR return akin to the UAE/GCC regimes, but GAFI and the ETA require substantive premises, payroll, and bank activity when issuing tax cards, treaty clearances, or Investment Law incentives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating contract revenue, creating false subcontractor invoices, routing mobilization payments through a dormant offshore shell, or commencing site works without registering the Egyptian permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment of 3 months to 5 years and a fine of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 under Article 134 of Law No. 91 of 2005, as amended. The ETA issues a full re-assessment for the evaded tax, plus the 2%-per-month deferment surcharge and CBE+2% interest. The court may order publication of the conviction at the taxpayer's expense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, signatories, and the resident representative are treated as principals and are jointly and severally liable for the evaded CIT and civil damages. The public prosecutor may impose a travel ban, freeze personal bank accounts, and, under Egyptian Penal Code veil-piercing rules, attach personal assets where the LLC is an alter ego of the accused.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / DTA Treaty Abuse / GAAR
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding the EPC LLC through a conduit with nominal share capital, no engineering capacity, no board minutes, and no operational risk; using the conduit to claim treaty-reduced WHT on dividends or royalties without beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA application of Article 36 GAAR and the MLI Principal Purpose Test: recharacterization of all flows as taxable dividends or royalties, denial of treaty benefits, additional CIT at 22.5%, surcharge, and interest. GAFI may strike off the commercial registration, and the entity is debarred from public infrastructure tenders for up to 3 years. Administrative fines up to EGP 500,000 apply for non-disclosure of real beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors face criminal prosecution for false declarations before GAFI and the ETA. Directors are civilly liable for the full revenue adjustment and legal costs. A travel ban and curatorship over the company bank account are imposed where the court concludes the structure exists solely for tax avoidance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving government bond escrow settlements into foreign shell accounts, making cash payroll payments above statutory thresholds, concealing beneficial ownership, or failing to report suspicious transactions to the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Law No. 80 of 2002, as amended by Law No. 75 of 2023: imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to EGP 5,000,000. The court may order confiscation of the serviced funds, cancellation of the LLC's commercial registration, blacklisting from the Egyptian financial market, and loss of VAT/CIT registration privileges for 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the designated compliance officer are personally subject to imprisonment and travel bans. Personal assets traceable to the laundering offense are subject to preventive seizure. Directors cannot transfer, encumber, or alienate property listed in the EMLCU freeze order until final acquittal.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exceeding the EGP 8,000,000 related-party threshold without a Local File; filing a Master File with fabricated comparables; charging an unlicensed head-office cost reallocation to the Egyptian LLC; or executing an intercompany loan at zero or non-arm's-length interest without an ETA agreement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA makes an upward adjustment to the arm's-length net profit and recharacterizes the excess as a deemed distribution subject to 10% WHT. The resulting additional tax attracts a 2%-per-month surcharge and CBE+2% interest. Defective documentation allows the ETA to substitute its own comparability benchmark and impose a fixed penalty of up to EGP 200,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative and expatriate site director are personally liable under Article 71 of Law No. 91 of 2005 for the unpaid tax balance. Courts may issue a travel ban against the general manager during the audit. Civil damages for the State's lost tax revenue lie jointly against the foreign parent's appointing directors, and repeated failure triggers criminal sanction under Article 134.
